title: One Point: The Horse is Hea Survives the Dawgs as Brock Bowers Watches From the Bench
dek: Sonny escapes Kai 122.7 to 121.7, three teams hit 3-0, and Randy does the unthinkable and makes a trade.
body: The closest game of the season so far was decided by exactly one point, and the deciding factor never left the bench. Sonny's The Horse is Hea beat Mekhi's Dawgs 122.7 to 121.7, while Brock Bowers sat in Kai's reserves and posted 22.6 points on an 11.15 projection. Swap him into the lineup and the Dawgs win by more than 20. Instead Mekhi falls to 0-3, and the guy with the deepest football knowledge in the league is left staring at a box score that will haunt his group chat for a week.

The bitter part for the Dawgs is how much went right. Tyler Shough, added off the wire this week for Jameson Williams, threw for 23.8 points on an 18.88 projection, the kind of pickup that reminds everyone why Kai's waiver instincts are feared. Justin Jefferson undid a lot of that work with 4.2 on a 14.79 projection. On the other side, Jaxon Smith-Njigba kept being the best thing that has happened to Sonny's roster, dropping 30.36 on a 17.19 projection after last week's 38. The model doubled down on the Horse, lifting its title odds from 10% to 21%, second in the league.

Up top, Ramon just keeps rolling. No Banner only HULK beat Kaushal's Habibsters 134.46 to 100.74, a 33.72-point win as a 77% favorite, and Brucie now has 444.2 points through three weeks, 72.6 more than anyone else. Matthew Stafford sat on the bench again and scored 20.9, which at this point feels less like a mistake and more like a flex. Habib got 23.9 from Drake London on a 12.52 projection, but 0-3 is 0-3, and the two-time champ is now looking up at five teams. His week on the wire was busy again: LaPorta in for Wan'Dale Robinson, the 49ers D/ST in for the Buccaneers, and Deebo Samuel Sr. back on the roster at the expense of kicker Jake Bates.

Philly got his second straight win, beating Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 117.88 to 100.98, and he did it with a two-man show. Jahmyr Gibbs went for 37.9, the top score of the week, and Brock Purdy added 31.28, which more than covered for De'Von Achane's 1.7 on a 17.27 projection. Harold Fannin Jr. scored 20.6 from Alan's bench, so the margin could have been bigger. Oddly, the model dropped Team Pillbert from 13% to 9% title odds after a win; the computer apparently noticed who's next on the schedule. JMoney deserves a nod too: 100.98 is his first triple-digit week of the season, even if 0-3 and 1% playoff odds don't care.

Zoe's first fantasy Bears-versus-Packers showdown went to the Chicago side, and the Wisconsin contingent will be reminded of that at every opportunity. Randy's The fumblers won the lowest-scoring game of the week 91.64 to 86.64, surviving Jonathan Taylor's 8.2 on a 19.1 projection. Bijan Robinson gave Zilgit 34.3 on a 17.31 projection, the second-best performance of the week, and as a 32% underdog she lost by just five. Z² also reshuffled hard, swapping Brian Thomas Jr. for Josh Downs, Jonathon Brooks for Blake Corum and Cairo Santos for Trey Smack at kicker, the moves of a manager who is not waiting around at 1-2.

The trade log finally woke up, and it woke up in the strangest possible place. Randy, a man who historically treats his roster like a vault, sent Javonte Williams to Team Pillbert for Stefon Diggs. Elsewhere, the two unbeatens did business: Sonny landed Chuba Hubbard from Ramon, who got Rashee Rice in return. Alan also added Bryce Young and Denzel Boston while cutting Jaxson Dart and the Lions D/ST, and in a small bit of comedy, Jordan dropped the Eagles D/ST and Sonny promptly picked it up.

The standings now have a three-team ceiling: No Banner only HULK, The Horse is Hea and The fumblers are all 3-0, with playoff odds of 100%, 96% and 92%. Team Pillbert sits alone in fourth at 2-1 with 76%, Ghostu-Spider SZN is fifth at 1-2, and three 0-3 teams fill out the bottom. Randy's title odds slid from 21% to 16% despite the win, the second straight week the model has docked him for winning ugly. The fumblers have 361.8 points, 82.4 behind Brucie, and that gap is what the computer keeps staring at.

Week 4 opens with the heavyweight bout: Philly's Team Pillbert against the undefeated HULK, a chance for Alan to prove the model's early faith or confirm its latest doubts. Zoe gets Sonny in a game she needs far more than he does, Randy draws a winless Habibsters team that has to snap out of it, and the Dawgs meet Counting or not Counting GV in a battle of 0-3 teams where somebody finally gets off the schneid. Somebody leaves that one 1-3, and somebody leaves it 0-4 with eleven weeks left to think about it.

social.text: Week 3 final: Team Pillbert 117.88, Counting or not Counting GV 100.98. No Banner only HULK 134.46, Habibsters 100.74. The Horse is Hea 122.7, Dawgs 121.7. The fumblers 91.64, Ghostu-Spider SZN 86.64. Three teams remain unbeaten at 3-0.

social.author: Dana Whitfield
social.text: Trade alert: The fumblers acquire Stefon Diggs from Team Pillbert for Javonte Williams. Separately, The Horse is Hea lands Chuba Hubbard from No Banner only HULK in exchange for Rashee Rice. Two deals in one week.

social.author: The Horse is Hea
social.text: 3-0! Won by a single point, and we'll take it. Player of the week: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, 30.36. And a warm welcome to the stable, Chuba Hubbard. 🐎

social.author: Gridiron Gary
social.text: Gibbs 37.9 plus Purdy 31.28 is a whole team by itself. Achane gave Philly 1.7 and he still won by 17. Pillbert vs HULK next week is appointment viewing.

bios.1: Sonny is 3-0 after a one-point escape against the Dawgs, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba scoring 30-plus for the second straight week. Title odds jumped from 10% to 21%, and Chuba Hubbard just joined the backfield. The reigning champ is starting to look like one.
bios.2: Randy is 3-0 and has won ugly twice in a row, and the model has docked him both times, down to 16% title odds. The big news is off the field: he actually traded, landing Stefon Diggs for Javonte Williams. A winless Habibsters team is up next.
bios.3: JMoney cracked 100 points for the first time this season but is still 0-3 with 1% playoff odds and the league's lowest point total. Tank Bigsby and the Patriots D/ST are the newest arrivals. Week 4 against the winless Dawgs is a genuine chance for a first win.
bios.4: Philly has won two straight behind a monster week from Jahmyr Gibbs and Brock Purdy. Even so, the model cut his title odds to 9%, maybe because the HULK is up next. A win there would make Team Pillbert the league's most dangerous 3-1 team.
bios.5: Kai is 0-3 after losing by one point with Brock Bowers' 22.6 on the bench. The waiver magic is real, with Tyler Shough paying off immediately, and the Dawgs have more points than two teams above them. A meeting with JMoney is the best chance yet to get on the board.
bios.6: Habib is 0-3 with 12% playoff odds after running into the HULK buzzsaw. Drake London showed up, and LaPorta and Deebo are the latest additions to a constantly rotating roster. The two-time champ draws an unbeaten fumblers team next, which is not the softest place to start a comeback.
bios.7: Ramon is 3-0 with 444.2 points, 72.6 clear of the field, and still benching 20-point quarterbacks. The model has the HULK at 52% to win it all and a 100% playoff lock. Brucie added Rashee Rice in a deal with Sonny, which feels unfair to everyone else.
bios.8: Zoe dropped a five-point heartbreaker to Randy despite 34.3 from Bijan Robinson and sits at 1-2 with 10% playoff odds. She reworked the roster with Josh Downs, Blake Corum and Trey Smack. Beating Sonny next week would put her right back in the race.
